**Typography & font terminology**
- Never say `typeface` — always `font`. Never say `type size` — always `font size` or just `size`. (Affects any UI copy or code comments.)

---

## Additional Rules from Full Apple Style Guide (June 2025)

### **Font Terminology**

| Avoid | Use Instead |
|-------|-------------|
| `typeface` | `font` |
| `type size` | `font size` or just `size` |
| `type style` | `font style` or just `style` |
| `typestyle` | `font style` |
| `typeface attribute` | `font style` |

### **Italic vs Italics**

- `italic` — adjective: "use italic text", "italic font style"
- `italics` — noun (always plural): "use italics to emphasize", "the italics are applied"
- Never: "use italics text" or "an italics style"

**When to use italics in UI copy:**
- Document/work titles
- Letters as letters, words as words (`the word restart`, `the letter i`)
- Emphasis (use sparingly)
- Placeholder names (`[app name]`, `[volumeName]`)
- Terms being defined (`INIT stands for *initialize*`)
- Variables in technical notation

**When NOT to use italics:**
- Text the user actually types — use quotation marks or code font instead
- Onscreen element names in title-style capitalization — use plain text

### **Capitalization: Sentence-style vs Title-style**

**Sentence-style** (Apple default for UI labels, eyebrows, descriptive text):
- Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns/adjectives
- Use for: nav labels, filter chips, status tags, footer text, form labels, tooltips

**Title-style** (for button labels and section headings):
- Capitalize: first word, last word, nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, conjunctions (non-coordinating), prepositions ≥5 letters
- Don't capitalize: articles (`a`, `an`, `the`), coordinating conjunctions (`and`, `but`, `or`, `nor`, `for`, `yet`, `so`), `to` in infinitives, `as` (any part of speech), prepositions ≤4 letters (`at`, `by`, `for`, `from`, `in`, `of`, `on`, `to`, `up`, `with`)
- Exception: always capitalize prepositions that are part of a phrasal verb (`Turn On`, `Log In`, `Start Up`)

**Button labels always use title-style.** Examples:
- "Enter the Dominion" not "Enter the dominion"
- "Read the Writings" not "Read the writings"
- "Add to Favorites" not "Add to favorites"

### **Dashes**

| Dash | Character | Use | Spacing |
|------|-----------|-----|---------|
| Em dash | — | Interruption, parenthetical aside, list mid-sentence | No spaces — close up to adjacent words |
| En dash | – | Number ranges, compound adjectives with two-word element | No spaces — close up |
| Hyphen | - | Compound adjectives before noun, prefixes with exceptions | No spaces |

```
Correct:  See all your schedules—work, school, and social—in one app.
Correct:  bits 3–17,  2003–2005
Correct:  desktop interface–specific instructions
Incorrect: See all your schedules — work, school, and social — in one app.
```

### **Quotation Marks**

- Always curly/smart quotes (`"` `"`) in UI text — never straight (`"`)
- Periods and commas go **inside** closing quote marks
- Semicolons, colons, `?`, `!` go **outside** unless part of the actual quotation
- Use quotation marks to enclose sentence-style onscreen element names in documentation
- Use italics (not quotes) for terms being defined after *called*, *named*, *termed*, *stands for*
- Use the `…` ellipsis character — not three separate periods

### **Ellipsis**

- Use the single `…` character (not `...`) to prevent awkward line breaks between dots
- If a menu item or button name ends with `…`, omit it in running prose:
  - Correct: "Choose File > New and click a template."
  - Incorrect: "Choose File > New… and click a template."

### **Buttons & Links**

- Button labels: title-style capitalization
- "Click a link" — not "follow a link"
- "Click" for mouse/trackpad onscreen elements; "press" for physical/mechanical keys and buttons; "tap" for touchscreens
- Never: "hit", "push", "type" for keyboard keys (use "press")
- Never: "click on" — just "click"
- Don't use "click and drag" — you either click or drag

### **Web Terminology**

| Term | Rule |
|------|------|
| `homepage` | Entry point page only — not the whole site |
| `webpage` | One word; a single document within a site |
| `website` | The whole collection of pages |
| `web` | Lowercase (short for World Wide Web) |
| `web app`, `web browser`, `web server` | Two words |
| `webcam`, `webcast`, `webinar`, `webmail`, `webpage`, `website` | One word |
| `landing page`, `portal` | Don't use — use `homepage` |

### **Lists**

- Precede all lists with a colon (even if the intro is a partial sentence)
- All list items start with a capital letter (except product names that begin lowercase)
- List items that are complete sentences end with a period
- List items that are fragments: no terminal punctuation, or consistent punctuation throughout

name: apple-css-style
description: Apple Style Guide rules relevant to CSS, UI copy, and web dev — sourced from full June 2025 guide
metadata:

Full rules live in `d:\IceBerg\DESIGN.MD`. This is a quick-reference summary of the additions extracted from the full Apple Style Guide (June 2025, 243 pages).

## Font terminology
- Always `font`, never `typeface`
- Always `font size` or `size`, never `type size`
- Always `font style` or `style`, never `type style` or `typestyle`

## Italic usage
- `italic` = adjective ("italic text"); `italics` = noun ("use italics")
- Use italics for: document titles, letters/words as themselves, emphasis (sparingly), placeholder names, variables, terms being defined
- Do NOT use italics for: text the user types (use quotes/code font), onscreen title-style element names

## Capitalization
- **UI labels, eyebrows, tags, footers** → sentence-style (first word + proper nouns only)
- **Button labels, section headings** → title-style (capitalize nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, conjunctions except coordinating, prepositions ≥5 letters)
- Title-style don't capitalize: `a`, `an`, `the`, `and`, `but`, `or`, `nor`, `for`, `yet`, `so`, `to` (infinitive), `as`, prepositions ≤4 letters
- Exception: always capitalize prepositions in phrasal verbs (`Turn On`, `Log In`, `Start Up`)

## Dashes
- Em dash (—): no spaces, close up to words — for interruption/aside
- En dash (–): no spaces, for number ranges and two-word compound adjectives
- Never use spaced em dashes ( — )

## Quotation marks
- Always curly/smart quotes in UI text (`"` `"`)
- Periods and commas inside closing quote
- Semicolons, colons, `?`, `!` outside unless part of quoted content
- Use italics (not quotes) for terms being defined

## Ellipsis
- Use single `…` character, not three dots `...`
- Omit trailing `…` from menu/button names when writing about them in prose

## Buttons & interactions
- Button labels: title-style caps always
- "Click a link" not "follow a link"
- "Click" (mouse), "press" (physical keys/buttons), "tap" (touchscreen)
- Never: "hit", "push", "type" for keys
- Never: "click on" — just "click"
- Never: "click and drag" — you click OR drag

## Web terminology
- `homepage` = entry point page only, not whole site; never `landing page` or `portal`
- `webpage` = one word
- `website` = whole collection
- `web` = lowercase
- `web app`, `web browser`, `web server` = two words
- `webcam`, `webcast`, `webmail`, `webpage`, `website` = one word

## Lists
- Always precede with a colon
- All items start with capital letter
- Complete-sentence items end with period; fragment items: consistent punctuation throughout

# Uriel — Auriel Solaris

Character portfolio site for **Uriel**, a Throne-class angel and the central figure of Auriel Solaris's two-timeline book series. Built as a single-page application with full client-side routing.

---

## Tech stack

| Tool | Version | Role |
|------|---------|------|
| [SolidJS](https://solidjs.com) | ^1.9.5 | UI framework |
| [@solidjs/router](https://github.com/solidjs/solid-router) | ^0.16.1 | Client-side routing |
| [Vite](https://vitejs.dev) | ^6.3.5 | Build tool & dev server |
| [vite-plugin-solid](https://github.com/solidjs/vite-plugin-solid) | ^2.11.6 | SolidJS Vite integration |
| TypeScript | via Vite | Type checking |

**Fonts** (Google Fonts): Playfair Display · Cormorant Garamond · Inter

---

## Project structure

```
IceBerg/
├── index.html              # Entry point — loads Google Fonts, mounts root
├── vite.config.ts          # Vite + SolidJS plugin config
├── tsconfig.json
├── package.json
│
├── src/
│   ├── index.tsx           # Router setup — all 6 routes defined here
│   ├── index.css           # Shared design tokens + page-header/footer classes
│   ├── vite-env.d.ts       # Vite client type reference (allows CSS imports)
│   │
│   ├── App.tsx             # Home page — three-column locked viewport layout
│   ├── home.css
│   │
│   └── pages/
│       ├── Timelines.tsx   # Two-timeline beat-by-beat comparison
│       ├── timelines.css
│       ├── Connections.tsx # Character web with filter + detail panel
│       ├── connections.css
│       ├── Books.tsx       # Published and forthcoming works
│       ├── books.css
│       ├── Worldbuilding.tsx  # Lore encyclopedia with sidebar nav
│       ├── worldbuilding.css
│       ├── Audience.tsx    # Contact / reach the author
│       └── audience.css
│
├── DESIGN.MD               # Full design guide — typography, CSS conventions, Apple style rules
├── CLAUDE.MD               # Claude Code project instructions
└── apple-style-guide.pdf   # Source reference — Apple Style Guide June 2025
```

---

## Pages

| Route | Page | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `/` | Home | Hero layout — Uriel's name, epithet, attributes, nav |
| `/timelines` | Timelines | Timeline A vs B beat cards with expandable detail |
| `/connections` | Connections | Filterable character cards with relationship panel |
| `/books` | Books | Four volumes across two timelines |
| `/worldbuilding` | Worldbuilding | Lore entries — dimensions, angels, hell, wings |
| `/audience` | Audience | Contact links for Auriel Solaris |

---

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:5173`.

```bash
npm run build    # Output to dist/
npm run preview  # Preview the production build locally
```

---

## Design

The site follows a warm amber/gold palette (`#fffbf0` → `#78350f`) with a three-font system:

- **Playfair Display** — hero name only (weight 600 italic)
- **Cormorant Garamond** — all headings, titles, quotes, descriptions (weight 300–400)
- **Inter** — body text, labels, nav, UI elements (weight 400–600)

All CSS is split per page to prevent bloat. Shared tokens and layout classes live in `src/index.css`. Full conventions are documented in `DESIGN.MD`.

---

## Author

**Auriel Solaris** · [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/auriel.solaris) · [REDACTED_EMAIL]
